identity.name: AMANTA HEALTHCARE LIMITED
identity.industry: Pharma / Sterile Liquid Packaging & Specialized IV Solutions

summary.oneLiner: Amanta delivered strong FY26 profitability with 42% PAT growth driven by operational leverage and debt reduction, and is now poised for a major inflection in FY27 with SteriPort capacity doubling to 12 crore bottles/year and a 10.8 MW solar project commissioning, which will drive EBITDA margin expansion to 24-25% and reduce finance costs significantly.

one-line thesis: Amanta delivered strong FY26 profitability with 42% PAT growth driven by operational leverage and debt reduction, and is now poised for a major inflection in FY27 with SteriPort capacity doubling to 12 crore bottles/year and a 10.8 MW solar project commissioning, which will drive EBITDA margin expansion to 24-25% and reduce finance costs significantly.
financial scorecard: revenue: +5% YoY to INR288cr; EBITDA/margin: stable at 22% (INR63cr); PAT (rptd): +42% YoY to INR15cr; PAT (normalized): +42% YoY (no major one-offs); order book: no formal order book, 3-6 month visibility; net debt: reduced from INR234cr (Mar'26) to INR204cr (May'26) due to debt refinancing and repayments
guidance: revenue growth: +30-40% YoY in FY27 (driven by SteriPort); margin: 24-25% EBITDA; order inflow: 3-6 month visibility; capex/commissioning: SteriPort Line 3 (commissioning by June 20, 2026); SVP line (Oct-Dec 2026); solar (commissioned May 25-30, 2026)
order book & pipeline: No formal long-term order book; 3-6 month visibility in key export markets (Thailand, UK, Philippines, Sudan); domestic demand driven by hospital-level purchasing without long-term contracts
segment / subsidiary detail: SteriPort: 42% of revenue, 27% EBITDA margin; SVP: 20% of SVP revenue (inhalation & ophthalmics); export: 39% of total revenue in FY26; domestic: 61%; conventional bottles: declining share
growth verticals / optionality: SteriPort capacity expansion (6.6cr → 12cr bottles/year); SVP line commissioning (inhalation & preservative-free ophthalmics); 20 products in pipeline; entry into regulated markets (UK already established); potential for higher-margin export growth
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin to expand to 24-25% in FY27 due to SteriPort scale (27% margin), solar savings (INR75L/month), and debt reduction; raw material (polymer) prices up 60-70%, fully passed on via 5-6% price hikes with no margin erosion
capex / expansion: INR110-120cr total capex for SteriPort Line 3 (completed); INR20-25cr for SVP line (to be commissioned Oct-Dec 2026); INR40-50cr for 10.8 MW solar project (completed); no further major capex planned in FY27
capital allocation: Debt reduction (INR30-40cr to be refinanced at lower rates); capex for growth (SteriPort, SVP, solar); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on financial prudence and balance sheet strength
risks & watch-items: Raw material price volatility (mitigated by price pass-through); regulatory delays in new product approvals; competition in two-port segment (though SteriPort has technical edge); currency fluctuations in export markets
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and execution-focused; strong emphasis on operational efficiency, margin expansion, and financial prudence; proactive on pricing, capex timing, and regulatory compliance; tone reflects leadership in niche sterile packaging
non-obvious takeaways: SteriPort has zero fungal contamination complaints across 30cr+ bottles sold — a key trust differentiator; company avoids hospital contracts to retain pricing flexibility; NPPA pricing is same for all two-port systems, but SteriPort’s technical superiority (121°C sterilization, transparency) ensures market dominance despite no price premium

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
